retention.note: archive keeps it; the chat's deletion removes it

rows.description: One row per audited act: actor principal, kind, target ids, at, and at most one summary (schemas/11-activity-summary.json, 200 characters, hub redactor).

retention.note: until chat-deleted; archive keeps it (07 C-07.6)

rows.description: A chat stream event (07 C-07.1): a ring entry or reconciliation record after the connector's and the hub's audit projection, fields per C-11.18 (ids, state words, counts, times). Only its label fields hold words, and they pass the hub redactor and the 200-character cap.

retention.note: 30 days, which meets 07 C-07.6's at least 30 days; pruned from the front

rows.description: A machine stream event (07 C-07.1): connector and daemon lifecycle, heartbeats and facts changes, ids, states, counts and times only.

A denial (04 C-04.27, schemas/04-deny-record.json): a line of the connector's authority log shipped over 05's authority.log frame, or a hub-side refusal. Fields: ts, count, enforcer, principal, chat and machine ids, decision id, method, path without query, rule, level needed, reason, status, and for sink activity one template summary (hub redactor). Never a body or query (C-11.20).

retention.note: undelivered after 30 days: expired, sender told. Not backed up: held text must not outlive its deletion inside a backup.

rows.description: The words of a message queued at the hub for a chat (offline machine, phone, Home's delegated messages). Claude must receive them verbatim, so they are not redacted; after delivery they stay 7 days for the Queue panel and redelivery checks.

retention.note: a record restored from a backup whose text is gone expires, the sender told (C-11.14, C-11.24)

rows.description: What remains of a message after its text goes: msg_id, chat, sender, chars, files_count, state, times. The same keys web-chat's publicItem keeps (lib/server/domain/queue.js PUBLIC_MESSAGE_KEYS).

retention.note: deleted within one minute of the daemon accepting the message (07), not at the upload ok; a 429 is retried; an hourly sweep removes orphans

rows.description: A composer image attached to a hub-queued message: at most 5 MB, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, as the daemon's /api/attachments accepts. Uploaded through the relay at delivery and uploaded again if the daemon pruned it before the message was sent; deleted at the hub once the message is accepted (C-11.22).

The closed list contract 05 names: connector and Claude Code versions, agents-at-once cap, pause state, folders offered (06's folder object: id, real path and the home-masked display path), chats hosted. Deleted on Disconnect; Activity keeps the machine's id and name.

retention.note: 300 s, contract 05 C-05.2

rows.description: Kept only as a hash, single use, gone at use or expiry.

The hub's own relay log (C-11.19, formerly the hub-access-log row): one JSON line per relayed write, socket upgrade and socket close: ts, principal, machine, chat, method, path without query, status, bytes, duration, close code. Never a body, query, frame or credential. The connector's authority log is not this row: it stays on the machine and what it ships lands in deny-record and activity-entry (C-11.20).
The hub process's own errors and lifecycle lines: codes, ids, counts; each line passes the hub redactor.
A device's Web Push endpoint and keys, removed when the push service answers gone or the user removes the device.

retention.note: the hub sets a Web Push TTL of at most one day on each message

rows.description: A notification: ids plus one Activity summary, encrypted to the subscription (C-11.23).

State dots, Needs you, queue and activity badges, built from 05's status poll (GET /api/mirror/status, GET /api/asks and GET /api/health, read by the connector as a local caller through lib/client and cut to the fields schemas/06-chat-status.json names, C-11.15) and rebuilt after a restart.
Any request or response body the relay carries between a viewer and a chat's daemon, exports, previews, mirror attachments and live composer uploads included.
Every frame of a relayed socket: render, store:patch, pane:form, markdown, mirror:*, element:*, queue. Projected per socket by the daemon; opaque to the hub.
A dashboard daemon's own graph, store and element log on the hub VM, kept by web-chat's rules (pane state is not redacted there today). Mirror panes hold references, never copies (C-11.16).

Home's daemon on the hub VM: its pages, store and elements, under web-chat's rules. Its mirror follows web-chat's own retention rows (lib/server/mirror/retention.js:48-134 at 826442d6): no count cap deletes; the only deleters are claude-code-cleanup and disk-budget-bytes, unlimited unless the host sets at least 64 MiB in .web-chat/mirror.json; parsed-conversations-max 160 bounds memory only; 64 task, 64 agent and 32 workflow rows persist per session.

retention.note: Claude Code's own transcript cleanup on the hub VM (its cleanupPeriodDays setting)

rows.description: Home's Claude Code session files on the hub VM. What Home read from chats arrived through the relay at its level, so mirror text in it was redacted at the source machine.

retention.note: removal from the allowlist sets removed_at and keeps the row, so ids in Activity still resolve; v1 deletes no account

rows.description: A user (usr_) or service user (svc_, svc_home) account (03 section 2, C-03.16): id, the display name the account chose, roles, created and removed times. The display name is its only words and passes the hub redactor.
A sign-in identity bound to an account: the issuer and the subject (03 C-03.6a as A-03.1 amends it), unique per pair. Ids only.

retention.note: deleted when an admin removes it; the removal is an Activity entry and the account row keeps removed_at

rows.description: One entry of the allowlist every sign-in, OIDC or OAuth 2.0, is checked against (03 C-03.6, A-03.1 C-03.6a): the provider and the verified email the entry admits, the role it grants at first sign-in, who added it and when. The email is the only identifying text the hub keeps for a person: it is a match key, read back whole by the admin listing and never written into a summary, an event or a principal (C-03.4), so it does not pass the redactor.

retention.note: one row for the hub's life; restore-finalize bumps it after a restore, so every restored session ends (C-03.30)

rows.description: The hub-wide auth epoch counter (03 section 2): bumping it ends every user session minted under an older value (C-03.30).

retention.note: kept 7 days after its expiry, sign-out or revocation; at most 30 days absolute (phone) plus 7

rows.description: A user session (C-03.5, C-03.6, schemas/03-credential.json user_session): user, client, idp, auth epoch, the sha256 of its secret, times, device, revocation. Not backed up: a restore signs everyone out, and restore-finalize bumps the epoch as well.

retention.note: single use, 60 s; removed by the hourly sweep after use or expiry

rows.description: A surface ticket (C-03.5, C-03.10): user session, chat, origin, the sha256 of its secret, created, expires and used times. Not backed up: it is dead within 60 s.

retention.note: kept 7 days after it ends; never outlives its parent user session

rows.description: A surface session on one chat origin (C-03.5, C-03.10): user session, chat, origin, ticket, the sha256 of its secret, times, revocation. Not backed up, like its parent.

retention.note: kept 7 days after expiry or revocation; a service user key with a null expiry stays until revoked

rows.description: An API key (C-03.5, C-03.7): owner, name, creator, the sha256 of its secret and its display prefix, scope, times, revocation. Backed up, so keys survive a restore; the secret itself is never stored. Its name passes the hub redactor.

retention.note: at most 12 h, renewed by the connector; kept 7 days after it ends

rows.description: An agent token (C-03.5, C-03.12): chat, machine, agent session, the sha256 of its secret, times, revocation. Not backed up: the connector requests a new one.

retention.note: until revoked or its user is removed, then 7 days

rows.description: A device registration (C-03.5, schemas/03-credential.json device): user, registering session, label, times, revocation. Its Web Push endpoint and keys are the push-subscription row. The label passes the hub redactor.

retention.note: one connection, at most 24 h; kept 7 days after it closes

rows.description: A connector session, one authenticated connector WebSocket (C-03.9, the plan's link session): machine, opened, expires and closed times, connector version, close reason. Not backed up: the connector dials again.

retention.note: Disconnect revokes the credential and keeps the row, so chats and Activity still name the machine; machine-facts goes at Disconnect

rows.description: A paired machine (C-03.8, 05 C-05.3; its shell view is 10's machine row): id, name, who paired it and when, state, revocation. The name passes the hub redactor.

retention.note: a rotated-out or revoked key keeps its row and state, so it is refused as revoked, never seen as unknown

rows.description: A machine's Ed25519 public key (C-03.8, 05 C-05.7): the derived mky_ id, the raw 32-byte public key, state (current, retiring, held) and retiring_until. A public key only; the private key never leaves the machine.

retention.note: 300 s, with its code (05 C-05.2)

rows.description: A pending pairing beside its pairing-code row (05 C-05.1 to C-05.3): the offered public key, client nonce, proposed name, platform, connector version, the asking address and when it asked. Gone at binding or expiry; the bound machine's record and Activity keep what matters.

retention.note: archive keeps it

rows.description: A workspace (10's workspace row, C-10.14 structure): id, name, archived. The name passes the hub redactor.

retention.note: archive keeps it

rows.description: A project (10's project row): id, workspace, name, theme, archived, and the project defaults 04 reads (C-04.2). The name passes the hub redactor.

retention.note: archive keeps it (C-04.3 rewrites its grants)

rows.description: A chat record (10's chat row; 04 C-04.2 reads owner, project, workspace and state): id, title, workspace, project, owner, machine, scope, state, archived time. The title passes the hub redactor.
A dashboard record (10's dashboard row): id, title, owner, keeper chat, pins. Its surface is the dashboard-surface row; the table is empty in v1. The title passes the hub redactor.

retention.note: a revoked grant keeps its row with revoked_at; each change is also a hub stream record and an Activity entry (C-04.3)

rows.description: A grant on one chat (C-04.2, C-04.3): chat, grantee principal, levels, specifics, who granted it, times, revocation. Ids, level words and times only.

retention.note: also removed with its principal's account

rows.description: The last decision version per (principal, chat), which C-04.6 keeps monotonic. A counter only.

retention.note: a chat stream's row goes with its chat, a machine stream's with its machine; the hub stream's stays for the hub's life; restore-finalize re-mints each epoch (C-07.4)

rows.description: A hub stream's head (C-07.1 to C-07.6): stream name, epoch, latest and oldest seq. Its events are the chat-event, machine-event and hub-event rows.

retention.note: the hub stream's events stay for the hub's life, never pruned (07 C-07.6 as amended by A-07.1); archive and restore keep them

rows.description: A `hub` stream event (07 C-07.1, A-07.1 C-07.5a): the activity.<kind> event of an Activity entry that names neither a chat nor a machine (sign-ins, API keys, grants, devices, allowlist changes), ids, kinds, outcome and times. Its only words are the entry's summary, copied as 11 C-11.13 built it, which passed the hub redactor and the 200-character cap.
The durable source cursor the hub holds per chat and ring (C-07.10, schemas/07-cursor.json source): chat, ring, boot, seq, capture_seq, element_seq and surface_gen. Ids and counters only.

retention.note: the 24 hours of 10 C-10.11

rows.description: An Idempotency-Key seen on a write or execute request (C-10.11): principal, key, the request's sha256 and the first answer as the hub built it. For a relayed type (C-10.17) that is the outcome only (ok, type, the error code and daemon_status), never result.daemon or error.daemon: never a relayed body (C-11.9). Not backed up: a restore past its 24 hours makes it useless. A result that carried a minted secret (an API key's) is stored without it (C-03.5).
